lines.text: Hi there, take a seat. What are you coming in with today?
It's my lower back, mostly on the right side, and it's been grumbling for about three weeks.
When did it start, and was there anything that set it off?
I was lifting a bag of compost out of the car boot and felt it go.
Does anything make it worse?
Sitting in the car is the worst, anything over half an hour and I'm stiff as a board.
Any numbness or tingling in your legs or around the saddle area?
No numbness, but there's been a sort of tingling down the back of my right thigh, although I'm honestly not sure whether that's just my imagination, and it comes and goes.
Let me have a look at how you bend. Can you stand up for me?
Forward bending stops at about mid shin and brings the pain on, and leaning back is fine.
Your straight leg raise on the right is about 60 degrees before it pulls.
I think what's going on is an irritated joint in the low back rather than anything sinister.
For the next few days, keep moving little and often, and get up from your desk every 30 minutes, even if it's just to fill a glass of water.
If you lose feeling around your bottom or have trouble passing water, that's an emergency and you go straight to A and E.
Okay, I'll keep an eye on it.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and gently rock them side to side, ten times each way, morning and night, as far as is comfortable.
Pop back and see me in a week, sooner if the leg pain spreads below your knee.
Will do. Thanks very much.
Take care now. Mr Okonkwo, would you like to come through?
Afternoon. It's my left elbow, it's been killing me since I started painting the fence.
Right, have a seat and we'll start from the beginning.
